questions.text:
The number of states in the minimum sized DFA that accepts the language defined by the regular expression
(0+1)* (0+1)(0+1)*
is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex](0+1)^*(0+1)(0+1)^*=(0+1)^+[/latex]: every non-empty string. The DFA needs a non-final start state (for [latex]\epsilon[/latex]) and one final state that loops on 0 and 1.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Language L1 is defined by the grammar: [latex]S_{1}\rightarrow aS_{1}b|\varepsilon [/latex]
Language L2 is defined by the grammar: [latex]S_{2}\rightarrow abS_{2}|\varepsilon[/latex]
Consider the following statements:
P: L1 is regular
Q: L2 is regular
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=\{a^nb^n\}[/latex]: needs counting [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not regular (P false).
- [latex]L_2=(ab)^*[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular (Q true).

Answer: P is false and Q is true

P is true and Q is false
P is false and Q is true

questions.text:
Consider the following types of languages: [latex]L_{1}[/latex]:Regular, [latex]L_{2}[/latex]:Context-free, [latex]L_{3}[/latex]:Recursive, [latex]L_{4}[/latex]:Recursively enumerable.
Which of the following is/are TRUE?
I. [latex]\bar{L}_{3}\cup L_{4}[/latex] is recursivelyenumerable
II. [latex]\bar{L}_{2}\cup L_{3}[/latex] is recursive
III. [latex]L_{1}^{*}\cup L_{2}[/latex] is context-free
IV. [latex]L_{1}\cup \bar{L}_{2}[/latex] is context-free
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]\bar L_3[/latex] is recursive (so RE), and RE is closed under union [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] RE True
- II: a CFL is recursive, so [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] is recursive; union of recursive languages is recursive True
- III: [latex]L_1^*[/latex] is regular (so CFL); CFL [latex]\cup[/latex] CFL is CFL True
- IV: [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] need not be CFL, so the union need not be False

Answer: I, II and III only

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Checking each statement:
- P. Lexical analysis [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (iii) regular expressions (token patterns)
- Q. Top-down parsing [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (i) leftmost derivation
- R. Semantic analysis [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (ii) type checking
- S. Runtime environments [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (iv) activation records

Answer: P-iii, Q-i, R-ii, S-iv

questions.text: In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?
questions.solution:
This is Belady's anomaly, which happens with FIFO. LRU, OPT and MRU are stack algorithms: with more frames the set of pages in memory only grows, so faults never increase.

Answer: FIFO
